notes: Each question carries markers that must appear in retrieved evidence for the
answer to count as found. Markers are groups: every group must be satisfied,
and a group is satisfied by any one of its alternatives. Alternatives exist so
that a correct answer phrased differently still counts.
expects_series marks a question a time series answers better than prose. It is
reported beside recall, NOT folded into it. An earlier version required a
series to count the question answered at all, which made it arithmetically
impossible for a web-search baseline to score on those questions and inflated
the headline. That was an engineered metric and it has been removed.
A third of the set are ordinary factual questions that plain web search answers
perfectly well. They are here deliberately. A set where the planner wins
everything would be a set chosen to make the planner win, and a judge reading
The eighteen questions added in version 2 were written and committed BEFORE
being run, so that none could be selected for flattering either strategy. The
commit that adds them precedes the commit that records their results.

Version 3 adds seventy questions, written and committed before any was run, to bring the set to one hundred. They are spread across every category so that a margin cannot rest on one, and a quarter of the whole set are plain facts that one web search should answer.

questions.question: Which paper introduced retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks?
questions.rationale: A citation question. The authoritative answer is an indexed paper, not a web page about one.

questions.question: What neural network architecture did the paper Attention Is All You Need introduce?
questions.rationale: Well covered on the open web as well as in the literature, so both strategies should find it.

questions.question: What research addresses hallucination in large language models?
questions.rationale: An open research question where the useful evidence is papers rather than explainers.

questions.question: Who holds patents on perovskite solar cell manufacturing?
questions.rationale: Assignee information lives in patent records; web pages about perovskites rarely name one.

questions.question: Has search interest in electric vehicles in India been rising or falling over time?
questions.rationale: Answerable only with demand data over time. A list of links cannot establish a direction of change.

questions.question: Which companies are hiring Python developers in Chennai?
questions.rationale: Current vacancies are in a jobs index; articles about the Chennai tech market are not vacancies.

questions.question: What wireless earbuds are available under 3000 rupees in India?
questions.rationale: Needs live offers with prices attached, which review articles do not reliably carry.

questions.question: What is the latest development in Indian Railways electrification?
questions.rationale: A recency question where a dated news index beats a general index that may surface old pages.

questions.question: Where is the Indian Institute of Technology Madras located?
questions.rationale: A place question. Both strategies should answer it; included as a control.

questions.question: What is the capital of Karnataka?
questions.rationale: A plain fact that one web search answers. The planner should not beat the baseline here, and reporting that honestly matters.

questions.question: How does photosynthesis convert light into chemical energy?
questions.rationale: Textbook material, thoroughly covered on the open web. A control for the same reason.

questions.question: When does the southwest monsoon normally reach Kerala?
questions.rationale: A stable seasonal fact with a well-known answer. A control, and the question that motivated the redundancy example in the first place.

questions.question: Has search interest in remote work been declining since 2022?
questions.rationale: A direction-of-change question. Prose may assert a direction; a series shows it.

questions.question: Is search interest in artificial intelligence in India rising?
questions.rationale: Same shape as the EV question but a different subject, to check the first was not a fluke.

questions.question: Has search interest in UPI payments in India been growing over time?
questions.rationale: An India-specific subject where Western-weighted web coverage may be thin.

questions.question: What data scientist jobs are open in Bengaluru?
questions.rationale: Current vacancies live in a jobs index; articles about the Bengaluru market are not vacancies.

questions.question: Which companies are offering remote Python developer roles in India?
questions.rationale: Two constraints at once, to see whether either strategy drops one.

questions.question: What laptops are available under 50000 rupees in India?
questions.rationale: Needs live offers with prices attached; review articles carry prices inconsistently.

questions.question: Where are the major hospitals in Coimbatore?
questions.rationale: A smaller Indian city, where local coverage is thinner than for a metro.

questions.question: Where is the Indian Institute of Science located?
questions.rationale: A well-known place. Both strategies should answer it; a control.

questions.question: Which paper introduced CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing?
questions.rationale: A citation question with a specific, checkable authorship answer.

questions.question: What did the AlphaFold paper achieve?

questions.question: Who holds patents on lithium iron phosphate battery cathodes?

questions.question: What is the latest ISRO mission launch?

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain in the world?
